label: Ranked cut list, largest saving first: four of five 011 transports, 003's exit-code status table, 011's duplicate message model, 008's secret-matcher, 003's CI job, 011's channel-queue (P1/P2)

003's activity.rs re-derives a six-value status vocabulary from exit codes while 001's activity --json already emits seven group ids, so scheduled and recurring rows draw ? and cancelled and stale are never emitted: key the marker table by group id and delete the exit-code mapping (P1)

011's channel.ts owns a second message record and imports nothing from 010's conversation.ts, so the two shapes share only text and no phase owns the translation: shrink it to a transport envelope plus one toConversationMessage adapter in conversation.ts (P1)

008's secret-matcher.ts saves one text scan per stored value over a handful of values at the cost of a lifted module, a lifted test file and a notice entry, while findSecretLiteral already walks the map once: delete the module and REQ-013 (P2)
003's bots-tui CI job adds a Rust toolchain cache and a second language's failure surface for a binary one operator runs locally: keep the two path entries and drop the job (P2)

011's five transports are four more than the parity goal needs: cut to Telegram and terminal, move Slack, Signal and WhatsApp to Out of Scope, and reduce the test matrix from five transports to two (P1)

reason: Six word lists and one function; the alternative changes the prompt contract every phase shares, so the saving does not justify it
